article.story: SEATTLE -- — Steele Venters made nine 3-pointers and scored 35 — both career highs — to lead the Washington Huskies to an 82-69 victory over Utah Tech on Thursday night. Venters had 23 points to help the Huskies cruise into halftime with a 58-40 lead. The fifth-year senior only missed three from beyond the arc and shot 11 for 15 overall. Venters played three seasons for Eastern Washington before transferring to Gonzaga, where he played just 27 games because of injuries from 2023-26. Nikola Dzepina had 16 points, five rebounds and five assists for Washington. Reserve LeJuan Watts totaled 11 points and eight boards. Freshman Christian Gibson scored a season-high 26 points on 10-for-15 shooting with four 3-pointers for the Trailblazers (1-4). Owen Mackay had 16 points, Ethan Potter scored 14 and both players grabbed seven rebounds. Gibson hit a 3-pointer to get Utah Tech within 21-20 in the first five minutes, but Venters answered from beyond the arc and then hit four more 3s in the final 7:25 as the Huskies pulled away. Utah Tech got no closer than nine after halftime. Washington outshot Utah Tech 47% to 43%, making 12 of 27 from distance and 10 of 12 at the free-throw line. The Trailblazers shot 8 for 19 from distance and 9 for 14 at the foul line. Up next Utah Tech will host South Dakota on Sunday. Washington will play No. 21 BYU on Monday at the Maui Invitational. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
